meta.title: Chile — Santiago & Torres del Paine, December 2027
meta.dates: Dec 16–25, 2027 (continues — next leg not planned yet) · Miami → Santiago → Puerto Natales → Torres del Paine

route.name: Santiago
route.sub: 4 nights from Dec 16 (room ready on arrival) · Hyatt Centric Las Condes (points) · Uber, no car

route.name: Torres del Paine
route.sub: 5 nights · Cabañas Lago Tyndall, Río Serrano (self-catering)

blocks.title: Dinner at home
blocks.detail:
• Full dinner before leaving, so everyone can sleep right after takeoff.
• Light on sugar.

blocks.title: Showers, comfy flight clothes, final bag check
blocks.detail:
• Kids in soft clothes they can sleep in.
• All 4 passports in one pouch.
• Pack the 2 travel booster seats (Chile requires them under age 9 / under 135 cm — in Ubers too).
• Fleece + rain shell in carry-ons: Santiago is warm, Patagonia is not.

blocks.title: Uber XL home → MIA, American departures (Concourse D/E)
blocks.detail:
• ~10 min from Miami Springs; 20-min block for loading bags.
• No long-term parking needed (trip is 10+ days and the return isn't set yet).
blocks.notes: • ~USD 25 for Uber XL incl. tip — estimated.

blocks.title: American check-in and bag drop
blocks.detail:
• International flight: agent checks passports.
• Check booster seats as bags (free on American) or carry them on.

blocks.title: TSA PreCheck → walk to the gate
blocks.detail:
• PreCheck lane for all four.
• Confirm gate on the AA app (usually Concourse D).

blocks.title: Gate: water bottles, snacks, pajamas, teeth
blocks.detail:
• Refill water bottles after security.
• Kids change into pajamas in the gate restroom and brush teeth.
• No new movies once boarded — lights out after takeoff.
blocks.notes: • ~USD 25 for water and snacks — estimated.

blocks.title: Board AA957
blocks.detail:
• Boarding ~45 min before departure.
• Last bathroom stop at the gate.

blocks.title: American AA957 - MIA → SCL - Nonstop - 8h25m
blocks.detail:
• Departs 10:50 PM Miami, lands 9:15 AM Friday Santiago (Chile is 2 hrs ahead of Florida in December).
• Overnight: sleep right after takeoff — about 6.5 hrs of real sleep is possible.
• Economy, 4 passengers.
blocks.notes:
• Not booked — planning assumption from the seats.aero result you shared: 25,000 points + USD 25.60 per person, T fare class, 9 seats, nonstop, 10:50 PM → 9:15 AM (+1).
• 4 × 25,000 = 100,000 points + 4 × USD 25.60 = USD 102.40.
• LATAM also flies MIA–SCL nonstop overnight (alternative if AA space disappears).
blocks.flag: Dec 16, 2027 isn't in the award calendar yet (American opens ~331 days out, about Jan 19, 2027). Set a seats.aero alert for MIA→SCL, Dec 16, 4 seats.

days.title: Land Santiago → straight to the room → lunch and the historic center

blocks.title: Arrive SCL — immigration, bags, SAG agriculture check
blocks.detail:
• PDI immigration with US passports (no visa or fee). Keep the PDI entry slip — it's your hotel VAT exemption.
• Every bag is X-rayed by SAG: declare any food; no fresh fruit, meat or dairy off the plane.
• 75 min gate-to-curb is realistic for a family with checked bags.

blocks.title: Meet Uber XL at the app pickup area
blocks.detail:
• From: international arrivals hall.
• To: the signed ride-app pickup zone outside (follow the Uber app's pickup pin; ignore drivers soliciting inside the hall).
• Install the 2 boosters in the back seat before leaving.

blocks.title: Uber XL SCL → Hyatt Centric Las Condes
blocks.detail: • ~30 km on Costanera Norte (urban tolls are included in the fare), 35–50 min with Friday traffic.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 30,000 fare + CLP 3,000 tip ≈ USD 37 — estimated (Uber/Cabify airport rides in Santiago run CLP 15,000–35,000 depending on demand).

blocks.title: Hyatt Centric Las Condes — straight up to the room
blocks.detail:
• The room is already yours: the stay starts the night of Thu Dec 16, so there's no waiting for 3 PM check-in.
• Enrique Foster 30, El Golf — 2 blocks from Isidora Goyenechea's restaurant strip; rooftop pool with Andes views.
• Room: 2 Queen Beds (29–31 m²) — the only standard room that fits 4.
• Globalist: free breakfast for 2 adults + 2 kids at Amandine.
blocks.nights: 4 nights (Thu Dec 16 – Mon Dec 20; arrive Fri morning)
blocks.cancelBy: Standard Hyatt award: free cancellation until the hotel's deadline (usually 24–48 hrs) — confirm at booking
blocks.notes:
• Not booked. Book Dec 16–20 (4 nights) — the Dec 16 night holds the room for the 11:30 AM arrival.
• Category 3 since May 20, 2026 (moved up from 2). Standard room per night: 8,000 (lowest) / 12,000 (low) / 15,000 (moderate) / 17,500 (upper) / 20,000 (top).
• Planned at 15,000 × 4 nights = 60,000 points; possible range 32,000–80,000 depending on the tiers Hyatt assigns to Dec 16–19.
• No hotel tax on award stays; foreign tourists are also exempt from Chile's 19% VAT on paid hotel rates (show passport + PDI entry slip).
• The former Grand Hyatt Santiago left Hyatt (it's not bookable with points), so this is the Hyatt to use.
blocks.flag: You won't show up the first night — after booking, message the hotel (and add a note in the reservation) that you arrive Fri Dec 17 ~11:30 AM on AA957, so the stay isn't cancelled as a no-show. Also confirm the nightly tiers on hyatt.com (blocked automated checks).

blocks.title: Showers and unwind in the room
blocks.detail:
• Hot showers, fresh clothes, 90 min to decompress after the red-eye.
• Swap into summer clothes: high 80s °F and sunny this afternoon — sunscreen and hats.

blocks.title: Walk to Tip y Tap, Isidora Goyenechea 2922
blocks.detail:
• From: hotel entrance on Enrique Foster.
• Walk 1 block south to Isidora Goyenechea, turn right (west) and go ~500 m to No. 2922 (8–10 min).

blocks.title: Lunch — Tip y Tap, Isidora Goyenechea 2922
blocks.detail:
• Santiago sandwich-and-grill institution since 1975: churrascos, lomitos, 'a lo pobre' plates.
• Kids' section: churrasco or grilled chicken strips with fries/rice/purée.
• Easy first meal after the overnight flight.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (menu dated Aug 2024): Churrasco filete Tip y Tap CLP 12,900 + Lomo liso a lo pobre CLP 14,900 + kids' Churrasco niño con agregado CLP 6,500 + kids' Tiritas de pollo grillé con agregado CLP 6,100 = CLP 40,400.
• +10% for price increases since 2024 = CLP 44,440; +10% tip = CLP 48,884 ≈ USD 54.
• Menu prices include VAT — estimated (current menu not confirmed).

blocks.title: Uber to Plaza de Armas (historic center)
blocks.detail: • ~10 km west along Providencia/Alameda, 20–25 min. Boosters in.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 9,000 ≈ USD 10 — estimated.

blocks.title: Plaza de Armas and the Metropolitan Cathedral
blocks.detail:
• Santiago's founding square (1541): palms, the Cathedral, the Central Post Office and the old Royal Court building.
• Cathedral entry is free (hours vary — step in if it's open).
• Busy square: phones and bags close, kids within reach.

blocks.title: Walk to the Mercado Central
blocks.detail:
• From: Plaza de Armas.
• North 2 blocks on Puente to San Pablo / the cast-iron market hall (~5 min).

blocks.title: Mercado Central — the 1872 iron market hall
blocks.detail:
• Fish and shellfish stalls under the wrought-iron roof the kids can wander through.
• Look, don't eat — lunch is done; the restaurant touts get pushy.
blocks.flag: The market closes around 5 PM on weekdays — keep this before the rest of the walk.

blocks.title: Walk to La Moneda
blocks.detail:
• From: Mercado Central.
• South along pedestrian Paseo Ahumada past the Plaza de Armas to Plaza de la Constitución (~1.1 km, 15 min, flat).

blocks.title: Palacio de La Moneda — the presidential palace
blocks.detail:
• Plaza de la Constitución in front: guards in uniform, the flag and the white façade.
• Exterior only today (the changing of the guard is a morning event).

blocks.title: Walk to Cerro Santa Lucía
blocks.detail:
• From: La Moneda.
• East on the Alameda ~1.3 km to the Terraza Neptuno entrance at the foot of the hill (~18 min; shade on the north side).

blocks.title: Cerro Santa Lucía — Neptune fountain, castle, tower lookout
blocks.detail:
• Free hilltop park where Santiago was founded: stone stairways, the Neptune fountain terrace and Castillo Hidalgo.
• The last stretch up to the Torre Mirador is narrow, steep stone steps — hold the kids' hands; skip it if crowded.
• Views across the city to the Andes.
blocks.flag: Entry is free; the gate may ask visitors to sign in. Confirm summer closing time (usually early evening).

blocks.title: Walk to Emporio La Rosa, Merced 291 (Lastarria)
blocks.detail:
• From: Cerro Santa Lucía, Lastarria-side exit.
• Down the east side of the hill into Barrio Lastarria, then 2 blocks on Merced (~6 min).

blocks.title: Ice cream — Emporio La Rosa
blocks.detail: • Santiago's famous artisan ice cream: rose-petal, chocolate-chili, lúcuma (a Chilean fruit) and plain chocolate for the kids.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 4,500 per cup × 4 ≈ CLP 18,000 ≈ USD 20 — estimated (current price list not checked).

blocks.title: Uber to Happening, Av. Apoquindo 3090
blocks.detail: • ~8 km east back to Las Condes, 20–25 min.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 9,000 ≈ USD 10 — estimated.

blocks.title: Dinner — Happening, Av. Apoquindo 3090
blocks.detail:
• Classic Las Condes parrilla (grill), open daily 12:00–21:00 — no waiting for a late kitchen.
• No kids' menu: a breaded beef milanesa and the meatballs in tomato sauce work for the kids.
• Sides are ordered separately.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, Nov 2026 online menu): Bife de chorizo 400 g CLP 38,000 + Medallón de lomo CLP 33,000 + papas fritas CLP 10,000 + ensalada chilena CLP 6,500 + kids' Milanesa de lomo CLP 23,000 + kids' Albóndigas Patti CLP 20,000 = CLP 130,500.
• +10% tip = CLP 143,550 ≈ USD 160. Prices include VAT.
• Reservations recommended for Friday.

blocks.title: Walk back to the hotel
blocks.detail:
• From: Happening, Av. Apoquindo 3090.
• East on Apoquindo ~1 km, then left (north) on Enrique Foster 2 blocks to the hotel (~18 min, flat, well lit).

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 9:00
blocks.detail: • Next morning wake-up 7:00 AM.

days.title: Water-park day — Fantasilandia Splash Park → flamingos at Parque Bicentenario

blocks.title: Wake up and get ready
blocks.detail: • Swimsuits on under clothes; towels, sunscreen (SPF 50), hats, flip-flops and dry clothes in the day bag.

blocks.title: Breakfast — Amandine (hotel buffet)
blocks.detail: • Globalist breakfast for 2 adults + 2 kids.
blocks.notes: • Covered by Globalist breakfast.

blocks.title: Back to the room — sunscreen on, day bag packed
Uber to Fantasilandia Splash Park (San Bernardo)
blocks.detail: • ~40 km south via Costanera Norte and Autopista Central (Ruta 5 Sur), 45–55 min. Boosters in.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 29,000 + tip ≈ USD 36 — estimated.

blocks.title: Splash Park entrance — tickets, lockers
blocks.detail: • Buy tickets online in advance; rent a locker for phones and dry clothes.
blocks.notes: • Prices not published yet (the park opens Dec 2026). Planned at ~CLP 22,000 per person × 4 + locker ≈ CLP 90,000 ≈ USD 100 — estimated from Fantasilandia's 2026 weekend ticket (CLP 22,990 over 1.4 m / CLP 10,990 under).
blocks.flag: New park — check the Dec 2027 Saturday hours, prices and kids' height rules for each slide once posted. Fallback: Parque Bicentenario de la Infancia (40 free slides) in the morning, Hyatt rooftop pool in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Fantasilandia Splash Park — slides, wave pool, kids' splash zone
blocks.detail:
• Fantasilandia's new water park in Lo Herrera, the first stage of its new San Bernardo complex.
• Kids' play structures and lazy river for the 6-year-old; the bigger slides for the 8-year-old if tall enough.
• Reapply sunscreen every 90 min — Santiago in December is high 80s °F with strong UV.

blocks.title: Lunch at the park food court
blocks.detail: • Burgers, hot dogs, empanadas, fries — whatever the park's food court sells.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 45,000 for 4 ≈ USD 50 — estimated (no menu published yet).

blocks.title: More water park — wave pool and slides
blocks.detail: • Second session after lunch; shade breaks every hour.

blocks.title: Showers, dry clothes, out to the gate
blocks.detail: • Wet suits into the dry-bag.

blocks.title: Uber back to the hotel
blocks.notes: • ~USD 36 — estimated.

blocks.title: Uber to Parque Bicentenario (Vitacura)
blocks.notes: • ~USD 8 — estimated.

blocks.title: Parque Bicentenario — flamingos and black-necked swans
blocks.detail:
• Free city park on the Mapocho with lagoons where Chilean flamingos and black-necked swans live year-round.
• Short stroll on the lagoon paths, Andes views to the east.

blocks.title: Uber to Liguria, Av. Luis Thayer Ojeda 019 (Providencia)
blocks.detail: • ~4 km, 15 min.
blocks.notes: • ~USD 8 — estimated.

blocks.title: Dinner — Liguria, Luis Thayer Ojeda 019
blocks.detail:
• Santiago's classic bar-bistro: home-style Chilean plates (pastel de choclo, plateada) plus pasta and gnocchi for the kids.
• Saturday hours 10:30 AM–9:30 PM.
• The 'platos del día' board changes — prices below are from the current online menu.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, Nov 2026 online menu): Plateada asada con puré picante CLP 21,600 + Pastel de choclo CLP 15,800 + kids' Ñoquis a la italiana y pesto CLP 15,400 + kids' Filete de pollo sandwich CLP 12,800 + papas fritas CLP 5,600 = CLP 71,200.
• +10% tip = CLP 78,320 ≈ USD 87. Prices include VAT.

blocks.title: Uber back to the hotel
blocks.notes: • ~USD 7 — estimated.

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 9:00
blocks.detail: • Next morning wake-up 7:00 AM.

days.title: Cerro San Cristóbal — cable car, summit, funicular, Bellavista lunch → slide park

blocks.title: Wake up and get ready
blocks.detail: • Sneakers and a spare shirt for the kids (water area at Parque de la Infancia).

blocks.title: Breakfast — Amandine (hotel buffet)
blocks.detail: • Globalist breakfast.

blocks.title: Room time — pack day bags, start packing for Patagonia
blocks.detail: • Lay out the cold-weather layers for Monday so the morning is quick.

blocks.title: Uber to the Parquemet Pedro de Valdivia entrance
blocks.detail: • ~5 km, 15 min. Drop-off at Av. Pedro de Valdivia × Av. El Cerro (no cars inside the park). Boosters in.
blocks.notes: • ~USD 8 — estimated.

blocks.title: Walk to Estación Oasis, buy the all-day pass
blocks.detail:
• From: Uber drop-off on Pedro de Valdivia Norte.
• Through the main gate at Av. Pedro de Valdivia × Av. El Cerro; Oasis station is a few steps to the right.
• All-day pass covers the cable car, funicular and park buses.
blocks.notes:
• All-day unlimited pass (2025 posted prices): CLP 9,250 adult × 2 + CLP 7,000 child × 2 = CLP 32,500 ≈ USD 36 — estimated.
• Teleférico runs Tue–Sun from 10:00 (closed Mondays).

blocks.title: Teleférico Oasis → Tupahue → Cumbre
blocks.detail: • 6-person gondolas over the wooded hill; the city spreads out below with the Andes behind.

blocks.title: Cumbre — summit terraces and lookouts
blocks.detail:
• 360° view of Santiago and the snow-capped Andes; clearest in the morning.
• Shade breaks and water — it's in the high 80s °F by midday.

blocks.title: Funicular down to Pío Nono (Bellavista)
blocks.detail: • The 1925 funicular runs down the steep face of the hill.

blocks.title: Walk to Galindo, Dardignac 098
blocks.detail:
• From: funicular base on Pío Nono.
• South down Pío Nono 3 blocks, left (east) on Dardignac 1 block to the corner (~6 min).

blocks.title: Lunch — Galindo, Dardignac 098 (Bellavista)
blocks.detail:
• Bellavista corner institution since 1968 — Chilean home cooking: pastel de choclo, lomo a lo pobre.
• Bilingual English/Spanish menu.
• No kids' menu: chicken milanesa and fettuccine bolognese work for the kids.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, Jan 2026 menu): Pastel de choclo CLP 11,800 + Lomo a lo pobre CLP 14,900 + kids' Milanesa de pollo CLP 11,500 + kids' Fetuccine bolognesa CLP 11,800 = CLP 50,000.
• +10% tip = CLP 55,000 ≈ USD 61. Prices include VAT.
blocks.flag: Confirm Galindo's Sunday lunch hours closer to the date.

blocks.title: Uber to Parque Bicentenario de la Infancia (Recoleta)
blocks.detail: • ~3 km around the north side of the hill, 10–15 min. Boosters in.
blocks.notes: • ~USD 8 — estimated.

blocks.title: Parque de la Infancia — 40-slide hillside, treehouses, water-sphere forest
blocks.detail:
• Free Parquemet playground park built into the slope of Cerro San Cristóbal: a cascade of about 40 slides, treehouses, swings, musical games and a mist/water-sphere forest.
• Bring a change of shirt for the water area; shade under the almond trees.
• Open Tue–Sun (closed Mondays).
blocks.flag: Free entry; kids must be with an adult. Confirm Sunday hours closer to the date.

blocks.title: Bathroom, water refill, request the Uber
Uber back to the hotel
blocks.notes: • ~USD 10 — estimated.

blocks.title: Pack for Patagonia, showers
blocks.detail:
• Big bags ready to go tonight — Monday's Uber is at 8:00 AM.
• Warm layers in the carry-ons for the 50s °F and wind on arrival.

blocks.title: Rooftop terrace — last look at the Andes
blocks.detail: • Kids can swim if they want; adults enjoy the view before the trip south.

blocks.title: Dinner — Amandine (hotel restaurant)
blocks.detail:
• Easy last night: dinner downstairs, no ride needed.
• Contemporary Chilean menu.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 110,000 for 2 adult mains + 2 kids' plates incl. 10% tip ≈ USD 122 — estimated (menu with prices not found online).
blocks.flag: No viewable menu online for Amandine — get it from the hotel, or swap for a restaurant with a published menu.

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 8:00
blocks.detail: • Monday wake-up is 6:00 AM: lights out by 8:00 keeps the kids at 10 hrs.

days.title: Fly to Puerto Natales → big grocery run → cabin at Río Serrano

blocks.title: Wake up, dress in layers, last bags closed
blocks.detail: • Fleece + shell on the plane; Patagonia arrives windy and in the 50s °F.

blocks.title: Breakfast — Amandine (hotel buffet)
blocks.detail: • Globalist breakfast.

blocks.title: Check out, request Uber XL
blocks.detail: • Request at 7:50 so the car is at the door at 8:00; boosters in.

blocks.title: Uber XL hotel → SCL (domestic departures)
blocks.detail: • ~30 km on Costanera Norte, 35–50 min in Monday traffic.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 30,000 fare + CLP 3,000 tip ≈ USD 37 — estimated.

blocks.title: LATAM check-in and bag drop (domestic)
blocks.detail:
• Domestic check-in area of the terminal; bags checked to Puerto Natales.
• Boosters go as checked items or carry-ons (needed for the Natales truck).

blocks.title: Security → gate; buy lunch-to-go for the plane
blocks.detail: • LATAM domestic flights sell snacks only — buy sandwiches airside for the flight.
blocks.notes: • ~USD 30 for sandwiches and water — estimated.

blocks.title: LATAM - SCL → PNT - Nonstop - 3h18m
blocks.detail:
• Seasonal summer route (LATAM runs ~3 a day in high season).
• Sit on the left (A) side for the southern ice fields if the sky is clear.
blocks.notes:
• Not booked. LATAM's lowest one-way SCL→PNT fares were CLP 72,000–78,000 (~USD 80–90) for Oct–Dec 2026, without a checked bag.
• Planned at ~USD 200 per person with a checked bag in Christmas week × 4 = USD 800 — estimated.
• Points option: Delta SkyMiles books LATAM to Punta Arenas (PUQ) at 15,900 miles + USD 8 per person (seen for Dec 2026–Jan 2027) = 63,600 miles + USD 32 for four — but PUQ adds ~3 hrs of driving each way vs. Puerto Natales. No Delta award space was found to PNT.
• Sky Airline also flies SCL–PNT in season (Nov 2026: 9:25 → 12:42).
blocks.flag: Dec 2027 schedule isn't loaded yet — confirm the late-morning departure when LATAM opens the dates (~Jan 2027).

blocks.title: Arrive Puerto Natales (PNT) — bags
blocks.detail: • Tiny airport; bags come fast.

blocks.title: Pick up 4x4 pickup — PNT airport
blocks.detail:
• Toyota Hilux 4x4 double cab or similar — gravel roads in the park, strong crosswinds, and room in the back for 5 days of groceries.
• Before leaving: check the spare tire and jack, photograph every scratch and the windshield, install the boosters.
• Open doors facing away from the wind — gusts can bend them (often excluded from coverage).
blocks.notes:
• Not booked; Dec 2027 not searchable yet. Kayak (Nov 2026): Toyota Hilux 4x4 USD 67–108/day; pickup average USD 91/day, highest in January (USD 93).
• Planned: USD 110/day × 5 days (Dec 20–25) = USD 550 + additional driver and full-coverage add-ons ~USD 100 = USD 650 — estimated.
• Agencies at PNT include Sixt, Econorent, Chilean Rent a Car and Lucano; book early — 4x4s sell out at Christmas.
• If the next leg leaves from Punta Arenas, a one-way drop fee applies.
blocks.flag: Gravel damage (windshield, tires) is often excluded from basic coverage — check the policy and your credit card's coverage for Chile.

blocks.title: Drive PNT → Puerto Natales center
blocks.detail: • 7 km, 10 min.

blocks.title: Late lunch — El Asador Patagónico, Arturo Prat 158 (main square)
blocks.detail:
• Patagonian grill on the Plaza de Armas; menu has English descriptions.
• No kids' menu: the kids share a sirloin steak with mashed potatoes and rice.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, 2026 online menu): Bife de lomo liso 350 g CLP 22,000 + Bife de lomo vetado 350 g CLP 26,900 + papas naturales CLP 4,000 + ensalada chilena CLP 4,800 + kids: Bife de lomo liso 350 g (shared) CLP 22,000 + puré de papas CLP 4,800 + arroz basmati CLP 4,500 = CLP 89,000.
• +10% tip = CLP 97,900 ≈ USD 109. Prices include VAT.
blocks.flag: Confirm it's open Monday mid-afternoon (many Natales kitchens close 3:30–7:00 PM).

blocks.title: Grocery run for 5 days — Unimarc Puerto Natales
blocks.detail:
• This is the only shop: there's no store in Río Serrano, the park or Cerro Castillo, and Natales shops close for Christmas Day.
• See the 'Groceries — Unimarc, Dec 20' list (Lists lens): 5 breakfasts, 4 packed lunches, 3 cabin dinners incl. Christmas Eve, snacks, water.
• Buy a soft cooler bag (bolsa térmica) for lunches in the truck.
• Pan de pascua (Chilean Christmas fruit cake) for Christmas Eve.
blocks.notes: • ~CLP 210,000 for 5 days of breakfasts, lunches, 3 dinners, snacks and water + CLP 10,000 cooler bag ≈ USD 245 — estimated.

blocks.title: Fill the tank — Puerto Natales
blocks.detail:
• There's no fuel in Río Serrano or inside the park — fill to the top.
• The truck arrives full from the rental counter; this tops off after the drive into town.

blocks.title: Drive Puerto Natales → Río Serrano (route Y-290)
blocks.detail:
• ~80 km: north on Ruta 9, left onto Y-290 past the Milodón Cave turnoff, then ~60 km of gravel to Río Serrano.
• 1h40 — first views of the Paine Massif across Lago del Toro.
• Very little phone signal after the first 20 km; download offline Google Maps.

blocks.title: Check in — Cabañas Lago Tyndall (5 nights), unload groceries
blocks.detail:
• 2-bedroom cabin with a full kitchen, living room and underfloor heating, a 1-min walk from the Serrano River and ~10 min to the park's Serrano gate.
• Superior Bungalow: 1 full bed + 2 twins.
• Fridge first, then set up the boosters' spot by the door.
• Check-in window 3:00–10:00 PM — send the arrival time in advance.
blocks.roomType: Superior Bungalow — 2 bedrooms (1 full bed + 2 twins), kitchen
blocks.address: Río Serrano s/n, Torres del Paine, Magallanes
blocks.cancelBy: Not booked — choose a free-cancellation rate when Dec 2027 opens
blocks.notes:
• Not booked; Dec 2027 not loaded yet. Booking.com prices for 2 adults + kids 6 and 8 in one cabin: $490 for 2 nights / $735 for 3 / $980 for 4 (≈ $245/night) in Dec 2026 and on the furthest loaded date (Mar 27–29, 2027); the 2 nights spanning Christmas Eve (Dec 22–24, 2026) were $580.
• Planned at ~USD 1,300 for Dec 20–25, 2027 (range ~$1,225–1,400) — estimated.
• Children 4+ are charged as adults here (already in the quotes). No extra beds or cribs.
• Check-out by 10:00 AM.
• Confirm whether Chile's 19% VAT is included — foreign tourists paying in USD are usually exempt.
blocks.flag: Sold out for the same dates this year — book as soon as Dec 2027 opens. Ask for a cabin with working floor heating in both bedrooms.

blocks.title: Walk to De Agostini Restobar at the Río Serrano Hotel
blocks.detail:
• From: cabin at Lago Tyndall.
• Along the village road toward the big hotel (signed 'Hotel Río Serrano'), ~800 m, 10 min.
• Bring a jacket — it's windy and in the 40s °F after dark.

blocks.title: Dinner — De Agostini Restobar (Río Serrano Hotel)
blocks.detail:
• The hotel's casual fire-grill bar: burgers, sandwiches, empanadas, pastas — open to non-guests.
• No kids' menu: lemon pasta and beef empanadas for the kids.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, current online menu): Classic burger CLP 19,700 + Pulled Beef sandwich CLP 18,200 + kids' Lemon Pasta CLP 18,700 + kids' Beef Empanadas CLP 11,200 = CLP 67,800.
• +10% tip = CLP 74,580 ≈ USD 83.

blocks.title: Walk back to the cabin
blocks.detail: • Same road back (~10 min). Still light out — sunset is ~10:15 PM.

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 9:45
blocks.detail:
• Blackout check: sunset is ~10:15 PM — tape a blanket over the window if the curtains leak light.
• Make Tuesday's lunches tonight if the kids are still up.
• Next morning wake-up 7:45 AM.

days.title: Lago Grey — iceberg beach and the Grey Glacier boat

blocks.title: Wake up and get ready
blocks.detail: • Warm layers, hats, gloves and windproof shells — it's cold and windy on the lake.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the cabin
blocks.detail: • Cereal, yogurt, eggs, toast, fruit — from the Natales grocery run.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Pack lunches + water, load the truck
blocks.detail:
• Ham-and-cheese rolls, avocado, fruit, cookies, granola bars, juice boxes into the cooler bag.
• Refill water bottles (2 L per person on park days).

blocks.title: Drive Río Serrano → Hotel Lago Grey
blocks.detail:
• ~38 km of gravel through the Serrano gate (show the park pass QR) and past the CONAF headquarters.
• Watch for guanacos on the road.

blocks.title: Torres del Paine park pass — multi-day (Dec 21–24)
blocks.detail: • Bought online only, before the trip; download the PDF/QR and print a copy (no signal at the gates).
blocks.notes:
• 2026 fees: international adult multi-day (2–10 days) CLP 48,500 × 2 = CLP 97,000. The park's own site lists children under 12 as free; another 2026 source shows foreign children at CLP 25,000 multi-day.
• Planned conservatively at CLP 147,000 ≈ USD 163 (≈ USD 108 if kids are free).
• Tickets are date-specific and non-refundable.
blocks.flag: Buy once the Grey boat and cabin are confirmed — tickets can't be refunded or changed.

blocks.title: Check in for the noon sailing — Hotel Lago Grey reception
blocks.detail:
• Check-in opens 1 hr before departure; restrooms here.
• Free parking at the hotel (overflow at Pingo, 20 min walk).

blocks.title: Walk to the boat: Pingo suspension bridge → iceberg beach
blocks.detail:
• From: Hotel Lago Grey reception.
• Follow the signed path across the Río Pingo suspension bridge, then along the gravel beach where icebergs strand at the shore, to the boat landing at the far end (30–60 min depending on lake level; flat).
• Kids can touch the small grounded ice chunks at the waterline.

blocks.title: Grey III catamaran to the face of Grey Glacier
blocks.detail:
• 98-passenger catamaran with an enclosed, heated cabin.
• Sails up Lago Grey past floating icebergs to the glacier's blue ice wall (~30 m high).
• Eat the packed lunches on board (no alcohol on board).
blocks.notes:
• Round trip from Hotel Lago Grey. Oct 2027–Sep 2028 price: CLP 135,000 adult × 2 + CLP 80,000 child (5–12) × 2 = CLP 430,000 ≈ USD 478.
• Departures 9:00, 12:00 and 15:00 (later sailings only when earlier ones sell out). No minimum age; under-5s free.
• About 4 hrs total including the beach walks.
blocks.flag: Strong wind cancels sailings — Friday Dec 24 is kept open as the make-up day.

blocks.title: Walk back along the beach and bridge to the car
blocks.detail:
• From: boat landing.
• Same beach path and Pingo bridge back to the Hotel Lago Grey car park.

blocks.title: Showers, dry clothes
blocks.detail: • Wet gear on the heated floor to dry.

blocks.title: Serrano riverbank — skipping stones, wild horses
blocks.detail:
• From: cabin door.
• 1-min walk down to the Serrano River bank; flat gravel shore with the massif straight ahead.
• Free-roaming horses graze around the village — admire from a distance (they bite).

blocks.title: Walk to Qawasqar at the Río Serrano Hotel
blocks.detail:
• From: cabin at Lago Tyndall.
• Along the village road toward the big hotel (signed 'Hotel Río Serrano'), ~800 m, 10 min.
• Bring a jacket — it's windy and in the 40s °F after dark.

blocks.title: Dinner — Qawasqar (Río Serrano Hotel restaurant)
blocks.detail:
• Patagonian à la carte, open to non-guests: trout, hake, lamb, short rib, pastas.
• Kids' menu: grilled fish, crispy chicken, sirloin steak, pasta.
blocks.notes:
• Line items (verified, current online menu): Angus Short Rib CLP 35,900 + Rainbow Trout CLP 32,500 + kids' Crispy Chicken CLP 14,500 + kids' Pasta CLP 8,700 = CLP 91,600.
• +10% tip = CLP 100,760 ≈ USD 112.
blocks.flag: Reserve as an outside guest — hotel guests on full board fill it in high season.

blocks.title: Walk back to the cabin
blocks.detail: • Same road back (~10 min). Still light out — sunset is ~10:15 PM.

blocks.title: Pack Wednesday's lunches
blocks.detail: • Into the fridge for the morning.

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 9:30
blocks.detail: • Next morning wake-up 7:30 AM.

days.title: Salto Grande waterfall → Mirador Cuernos → Lago Pehoé

blocks.title: Wake up and get ready
blocks.detail: • Hiking shoes, layers, sunscreen.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the cabin
blocks.detail: • Cereal, yogurt, eggs, toast, fruit — from the Natales grocery run.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Lunches into the cooler, load the truck
blocks.detail: • Packed last night.

blocks.title: Drive Río Serrano → Pudeto (Lago Pehoé)
blocks.detail:
• ~45 km gravel along Lago del Toro and the Serrano valley, then around Lago Pehoé.
• Park at Pudeto (catamaran dock; toilets).

blocks.title: Walk Pudeto → Salto Grande
blocks.detail:
• From: Pudeto car park.
• Signed gravel path north ~1 km to the falls (15–20 min, flat).

blocks.title: Salto Grande — turquoise waterfall under the Cuernos
blocks.detail:
• Lago Nordenskjöld pours into Lago Pehoé here.
• Gusts at the viewpoint can knock a child over — hold hands near the edge.

blocks.title: Hike Salto Grande → Mirador Cuernos
blocks.detail:
• From: Salto Grande viewpoint.
• Continue on the signed trail ~2.5 km along Lago Nordenskjöld to the Cuernos lookout; mostly flat, some short rises.
• Turn around whenever the kids are done — the views start almost immediately.

blocks.title: Packed lunch at Mirador Cuernos
blocks.detail: • Sit in the lee of the rocks; the horned peaks are right across the lake.

blocks.title: Hike back to Pudeto
blocks.detail:
• From: Mirador Cuernos.
• Same trail back past Salto Grande to the Pudeto car park (~3.5 km).

blocks.title: Mirador Lago Pehoé — the postcard view
blocks.detail: • Roadside viewpoint ~10 min from Pudeto toward the park headquarters: turquoise Lago Pehoé with the Cuernos and Paine Grande behind.

blocks.title: Kids' downtime — cards, drawing, porch views
blocks.detail: • Adults start dinner prep at 6.

blocks.title: Cook dinner in the cabin — pasta bolognese + salad
blocks.detail: • Spaghetti, ground beef, tomato sauce, salad from the Dec 20 shop.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Dishes, pack Thursday's lunches
blocks.detail: • Thursday is the long drive — extra snacks in the truck.

blocks.title: Bedtime routine — lights out 9:00
blocks.detail: • Thursday wake-up 7:00 AM (longer drive).

days.title: East side — Laguna Amarga, Paine waterfall, Laguna Azul

blocks.title: Wake up and get ready
blocks.detail: • Binoculars for guanacos, rheas and condors.

blocks.title: Breakfast in the cabin
blocks.detail: • Cereal, yogurt, eggs, toast, fruit — from the Natales grocery run.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Lunches into the cooler, load the truck
blocks.detail: • Packed last night.

blocks.title: Drive across the park → Laguna Amarga
blocks.detail:
• ~75 km of gravel via Pehoé and Lago Nordenskjöld — the longest drive of the stay.
• Guanaco herds graze beside the road on the eastern steppe; pull fully off the road to stop.
• Fuel check: ~250 km since the Natales fill-up — well over half a tank in a Hilux. Today adds ~150 km.

blocks.title: Laguna Amarga ranger station — the three towers across the lagoon
blocks.detail:
• Show the park pass; toilets.
• First full view of the Torres granite spires.

blocks.title: Drive to the Paine River waterfall
blocks.detail: • ~8 km toward Laguna Azul.

blocks.title: Cascada Río Paine — short walk to the falls
blocks.detail:
• From: roadside car park.
• 5-min path to the viewpoint over the broad waterfall, the towers behind it.

blocks.title: Packed lunch at Laguna Azul picnic area
blocks.detail: • Best view of the three towers without trekking.

blocks.title: Laguna Azul lakeshore walk
blocks.detail:
• From: Laguna Azul picnic area.
• Walk the eastern shore toward the small lookout hill; flat, open steppe — easy for both kids.
• The microclimate here is often the warmest and calmest in the park.

blocks.title: Drive back to the cabin
blocks.detail: • Same route west; allow time for wildlife stops.

blocks.title: Showers, dry clothes; start a load of laundry
blocks.detail: • Mid-stay wash of base layers and socks (ask the cabin office about the laundry).

blocks.title: Cook dinner in the cabin — chicken, rice and vegetables
blocks.detail: • Chicken breasts, rice, carrots/peas from the Dec 20 shop.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Dishes; pack Friday's lunches (in case it's a park day)
Bedtime routine — lights out 9:30
blocks.detail: • Friday wake-up 7:30 AM.

days.title: Christmas Eve — weather make-up day, riding, cabin Christmas dinner

blocks.title: Breakfast in the cabin
blocks.detail: • Cereal, yogurt, eggs, toast, fruit — from the Natales grocery run.
blocks.notes: • Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.

blocks.title: Decide: make-up park day or ranch morning
blocks.detail:
• If wind cancelled Tuesday's Grey boat → drive to Lago Grey for the noon sailing (same plan as Tuesday; lunches already packed).
• If a park day was lost to weather → repeat it today.
• Otherwise → horseback morning below.

blocks.title: Horseback ride with a local baqueano (Patagonian ranch guide)
blocks.detail:
• Book with The Massif (the excursion operator based at the Río Serrano Hotel, a 10-min walk) — gentle ride on the Serrano ranch land with the massif in view.
• Riding is Patagonia's working culture; helmets provided.
blocks.notes: • Price not published online. Typical Torres del Paine 2-hr rides run ~USD 70–90 per rider — not included in totals until quoted.
blocks.flag: Ask whether non-hotel guests can book and the minimum riding age — if it's 8+, swap for a Serrano riverside walk.

blocks.title: Lunch in the cabin
blocks.detail: • Sandwiches and fruit.

blocks.title: Quiet time — wrap presents, cards, games
blocks.detail: • Chile celebrates on Christmas Eve night; the 'Viejito Pascuero' (Santa) comes at midnight for local kids.

blocks.title: Riverbank walk and photos with the massif
blocks.detail:
• From: cabin door.
• Down to the Serrano River and along the bank toward the hotel; turn back whenever the kids are done.

blocks.title: Fuel check — plan Christmas morning
blocks.detail: • No fuel in Río Serrano. If below a quarter tank, refuel in Puerto Natales on the way out on Dec 25 (check holiday hours) or at Cerro Castillo.
blocks.notes: • Refuel cost goes with the next leg (depends on where the truck is returned).

blocks.title: Cook Christmas Eve dinner — steak, mashed potatoes, salad
blocks.detail: • Lomo (beef tenderloin) and potatoes bought Dec 20; pan de pascua for dessert.
blocks.notes:
• Covered by the Dec 20 grocery shop.
• Option: if the Río Serrano Hotel sells its Christmas Eve dinner to outside guests, book it instead (Hotel Lago Grey charged CLP 98,000 per person for its Christmas dinner in 2026–27 — likely similar).

blocks.title: Christmas Eve dinner in the cabin
Christmas Eve — pan de pascua, a movie, stockings out
Bedtime routine — lights out 9:30
blocks.detail: • Christmas morning presents first thing.

Breakfast in the cabin

blocks.title: Pack, clean the kitchen, bag the trash
blocks.detail:
• Leftover snacks and water go in the truck for the drive.

blocks.title: Next leg — not planned yet
blocks.detail:
• Christmas Day is a national holiday: most shops in Puerto Natales are closed; fuel stations may run reduced hours.
• The truck return (PNT vs. Punta Arenas) and the onward flight depend on the next stop.

alternatives.title: Alternatives considered — Torres del Paine lodging and the Patagonia flight
alternatives.text:
LODGING (5 nights, Dec 20–25)
• Cabañas Lago Tyndall — PLANNED. ~$1,300 est. for 5 nights (≈ $245/night on Booking.com for all four, Dec 2026 / Mar 2027 reference dates). 2-bedroom cabins with a full kitchen and underfloor heating in Pueblito Serrano, next to the Río Serrano Hotel — same drives to the park. Self-catering: one big grocery shop in Natales, packed lunches, 3 cabin dinners, 2 dinners at the hotel restaurants. No pool.
• Río Serrano Hotel + Spa, full board — the original pick, dropped on cost: ~$7,750 est. for all four with every meal and box lunches, heated indoor pool. Same location as Tyndall.
• Airbnb — Serrano River 2-bedroom apartment next to the hotel ~$3,313; townhouse ('Spectacular apartments', Roberto) $5,645 all-in. Same location, more money than Tyndall.
• Cerro Castillo cabin ~$993 for 5 nights — cheaper, but ~1 hr farther from Grey/Pehoé each way.
• Puerto Natales Airbnbs $563–1,048 for 5 nights — cheapest, but 1.5–2 hrs each way to the park every day (6–8 extra hours of driving over the stay).
• The Singular Patagonia (Puerto Natales) — the only easy points option (World of Hyatt via Mr & Mrs Smith, dynamic pricing, no Globalist benefits beyond a possible upgrade). Every room maxes at 2 adults + 1 child, so it takes 2 rooms: $747 per room per night (member B&B rate, Mar 2027, the furthest high-season date loaded) → ~$7,470+ for 5 nights before Christmas-week pricing, plus dinners. 1.5–2 hrs each way to Grey/Pehoé/Laguna Azul every day. Points price couldn't be checked (hyatt.com blocked automated checks); at typical dynamic rates expect several hundred thousand points for 2 rooms.
• Airbnb — 'Spectacular apartments in Torres del Paine' (Roberto, Superhost, 4.86): 2 bedrooms by the Serrano River next to the hotel. $5,645 all-in for Dec 20–25, 2027, free cancellation before Nov 20, 2027. Same location as the hotel, but no meals (add ~$1,000+ for dinners at the hotel restaurant and groceries from Natales), thin walls and a very basic kitchen per recent reviews, no pool.
• Hotel Lago Grey — inside the park at the glacier lake; rooms take 2 people with no extra beds, so 2 rooms (~CLP 315,000–430,000 each per night with breakfast, 2026–27). Basic rooms, far from the eastern sector.
• Explora / Awasi / Tierra Patagonia / Las Torres all-inclusive — built around guided group or private-guide excursions, which you don't want; $3,000+/night.

FLIGHT TO PATAGONIA
• Planned: cash LATAM Santiago → Puerto Natales (~$800 for 4). PNT is 7 km from town and ~2 hrs from the cabin.
• Points: Delta SkyMiles on LATAM to Punta Arenas, 15,900 miles + $8 per person (63,600 + $32 for 4). Punta Arenas is ~3 hrs farther by road each way (~5 hrs to Río Serrano).

help.notes: Chile emergency numbers work from any phone. Cell signal is weak or absent across most of Torres del Paine — the cabin office or the Río Serrano Hotel front desk can call out.
